lesson.title: Hip joint stability and femoral head supply
lesson.summary: The deep acetabulum and labrum provide bony and fibrocartilaginous stability, while capsular ligaments tighten in extension.
tags: Hip joint stability and femoral head supply

steps.title: Hip Joint
steps.body: The hip joint is a multiaxial ball-and-socket joint between the femoral head and acetabulum. It sacrifices some mobility for stability through a deep socket, acetabular labrum, strong capsule, and spiral ligaments.

steps.title: Relationships and functional organization
steps.body: Surfaces: femoral head and lunate surface of acetabulum. Labrum deepens acetabulum. Capsule attaches to acetabular margin and transverse acetabular ligament proximally. External ligaments: iliofemoral, pubofemoral, ischiofemoral. Internal ligaments: transverse acetabular ligament and ligament of head of femur. Zona orbicularis encircles femoral neck.

steps.title: Why do the capsular ligaments become especially important in upright stance?
steps.body: The spiral arrangement of the iliofemoral, pubofemoral and ischiofemoral supports tends to tighten with extension, limiting excessive movement and helping stabilize standing with reduced muscular effort. Flexion relaxes parts of this capsular arrangement and permits greater mobility. This mechanical pattern differs from the shoulder's reliance on dynamic muscular centering around a shallow socket. The ligament of the head lies within the joint region but is not the principal adult restraint replacing those capsular supports.

steps.title: Apply the anatomy and resolve a common confusion
steps.body: The deep acetabulum and labrum provide bony and fibrocartilaginous stability, while capsular ligaments tighten in extension. Retinacular vessels ascend along the femoral neck and can be disrupted by displaced intracapsular fractures. The artery within the ligament of the head has a variable, usually limited adult contribution and should not be taught as the sole supply. Stability and vascular vulnerability are separate consequences of the same close neck-capsule relationship.
